ai.title: Fix base agent user spawning for non-spawning workers
ai.summary: The CLI agent registry now prevents custom user agents from being incorrectly added to the `spawnableAgents` list of base agents that cannot spawn subagents. The previous logic appended user IDs to any definition with an ID starting with `base` and a non-empty `spawnableAgents` array, which broke validation for fast-mode workers like `base3-fast-worker-deepseek-flash`. The updated condition requires the agent to explicitly support spawning via `spawn_agents`, `spawn_agent_inline`, or `handleSteps` before merging user agent IDs, ensuring non-spawning workers retain an empty child list.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies `loadAgentDefinitions` in `cli/src/utils/local-agent-registry.ts` to add a check that `def.toolNames` includes `spawn_agents` or `spawn_agent_inline`, or that `def.handleSteps` exists, before appending user agent IDs to `spawnableAgents`.

eli5.text: The assistant's planning mode now correctly separates the main orchestrator from its helper workers when you add custom agents. Previously, the system incorrectly assumed all components that start with a specific naming pattern could spawn new tasks, which caused validation errors for fast-mode helper agents. This fix ensures that only the orchestrator automatically includes your custom agents in its list of tasks it can delegate, while simpler workers keep their task lists empty. You likely notice no change in daily use unless you rely on these specific fast-mode workers, in which case the assistant will no longer crash or fail to start when loading your custom configurations.
